name: Jeroham
overview: Jeroham is a male member of the tribe of Levi noted primarily as the father of Elkanah and grandfather of the prophet Samuel. His role is significant within the Levitical lineage, which held priestly responsibilities in Israel. Beyond his familial connections, no additional personal details or notes are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeroham means 'he will be compassionate.' This proper name, as recorded in 1 Samuel 1:1, does not appear to have been given directly by God but reflects a meaningful attribute possibly valued by his family or community.
familyAndRelationships: Jeroham is explicitly identified as the father of Elihu and is inferred to be the father of Elkanah, making him the grandfather of Samuel. These relationships highlight his place within a significant biblical family line that produced key figures in Israel's history.
scriptureSignificance: Jeroham's importance in Scripture stems from his position in the ancestral line leading to Samuel, one of Israel's greatest prophets and a pivotal figure in the establishment of the monarchy. Through his son Elkanah and grandson Samuel, Jeroham contributes to the unfolding of God's redemptive plan as recorded in the Old Testament. His Levitical heritage underscores the priestly context from which Samuel emerged, emphasizing God's continued work through chosen families.
